question: A 63-year-old retired teacher presents to his family physician for an annual visit. He has been healthy for most of his life and currently takes no medications, although he has had elevated blood pressure on several visits in the past few years but declined taking any medication. He has no complaints about his health and has been enjoying time with his grandchildren. He has been a smoker for 40 years–ranging from half to 1 pack a day, and he drinks 1 beer daily. On presentation, his blood pressure is 151/98 mm Hg in both arms, heart rate is 89/min, and respiratory rate is 14/min. Physical examination reveals a well-appearing man with no physical abnormalities. A urinalysis is performed and shows microscopic hematuria. Which of the following is the best next step for this patient?

options.opa: Reassure the patient and recommend lifestyle modifications for his hypertension
options.opb: Perform a CT scan of the abdomen with contrast

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Microscopic hematuria" -> "Further evaluation needed" -> 90% CHAIN: "Microscopic hematuria" -> "Consider underlying causes" -> 85% CHAIN: "Microscopic hematuria" -> "Increased risk of underlying pathology" -> 80% CHAIN: "Microscopic hematuria" -> "Perform additional diagnostic tests" -> 90%
enhanced_information: Microscopic hematuria in this patient with a history of smoking and hypertension warrants further evaluation due to the increased risk of underlying pathology. The best next step would be to perform a CT scan of the abdomen with contrast to assess for possible renal or urologic causes.
analysis: Microscopic hematuria in a patient with a history of smoking and hypertension raises concern for underlying pathology, particularly renal or urologic causes. Given the enhanced information provided, a CT scan of the abdomen with contrast is the most appropriate next step to further evaluate the potential underlying issues. This aligns with the consensus that imaging studies are indicated in this scenario.
